rows.notes: The cited study is a systematic literature review (SLR) of 38 primary studies on drone-based plant disease detection; it reports no own experiment, survey, data or model runs, only tallies of disease types, drone types, image types, ML tasks and algorithms from the reviewed papers. It therefore cannot provide primary evidence that UAV/remote-sensing systems with AI classification improve diagnostics, optimise treatment strategies or support targeted agrochemical application. Even the reviewed studies concern detection/classification rather than treatment or targeted application, so the claim would be upstream relative to the review's subject matter; upstream not flagged because Q1 is already 'no'.

notes: Document is a complete systematic literature review (Chin, Catal & Kassahun 2023, Precision Agriculture). Figures are not reproduced in the text but the results tables and narrative are complete. No primary data reported.
